Hi Anita — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Dev (solutions/security) and Marcus (account lead) to provide the technical details. High level answers while they prep a short write-up: 

- In-transit: All traffic is TLS 1.2+ with mutual TLS available for Dedicated and Private deployments.
- At-rest: Default service encryption for hosted models; Dedicated and Private support customer-managed keys (BYOK) via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations for on-prem.
- Logs: We provide request-level audit logs (request timestamps, client id, route, model variant). Key usage logs come from the KMS provider (e.g., AWS CloudTrail entries for KMS ops) when BYOK is enabled. Retention windows are configurable for Dedicated/Private; hosted has standard retention "X days" — Dev will confirm exact numbers.

I'll attach our KMS architecture doc and SOC2 summary for your security team to review. Next step: Dev will send a slightly more detailed note about BYOK flow and any implications for latency/rollout. Marcus — can we schedule a 30-min technical review with FinPay next week?

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Anita — quick technical summary as requested (TL;DR at top).

TL;DR: Redwood supports TLS in-transit, AES-256 at-rest; Dedicated/Private allow BYOK via AWS KMS/GCP KMS or customer HSM (PKCS#11). Audit logs for key usage are sourced from the KMS provider; Redwood exposes request-level logs for inference events and can route audit logs to your SIEM via S3/CloudWatch/Stackdriver.

Details: 
1) In-transit encryption
- All customer-facing endpoints use TLS 1.2+; we support TLS 1.3 for lower latency.
- Mutual TLS (mTLS) is available for Dedicated and Private deployments for client auth.

2) At-rest encryption + BYOK
- Hosted: managed keys (Redwood-owned) by default.
- Dedicated/Private: BYOK supported — you can register a customer key in AWS KMS or GCP KMS and grant Redwood the necessary IAM/KMS grants. For on-prem/VPC HSMs, we support PKCS#11 HSM integrations and can work with your key lifecycle ops team.
- Key rotation: Supported via KMS; Redwood recommends rotating keys per your policy. Rolling re-encryption semantics depend on the deployment (we can provide a migration plan).

3) Key usage and audit logging
- Key operations (Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey) are recorded in the KMS provider audit logs (CloudTrail/Cloud Audit Logs).
- Redwood also emits per-request metadata (timestamp, request id, model id, customer id, route) to your logging sink; we do not store raw customer prompts in plaintext in long-term logs unless specifically configured for debugging/evals and approved by contract.
- Retention: For Dedicated/Private you choose retention; hosted has 90-day default for request logs but we can discuss extended retention as a paid option.

4) Data residency
- Requests can be routed to region-specific clusters. For EU residency, we will pin your traffic to EU region nodes. Cross-region failover is an option but will be explicit in the SLA and has compliance implications (we can disable cross-region failover if needed).

5) Performance/operational notes
- BYOK adds negligible encryption/decryption latency; however, HSM-based signing for certain ops can add small tail latency — we'll quantify in the technical review.

Attachments: redwood-kms-architecture.pdf (architecture diagram), soc2-summary.pdf (SOC 2 scope).

If useful, we can run a short proof-of-concept where we register a test KMS key and show audit logs flowing to your CloudTrail/SIEM. Proposed next steps: 1) 30-min technical review next Tue/Wed, 2) run POC for BYOK (2-4 days), 3) finalize contract language for key control & audit.

— Dev

1) For the BYOK flow with AWS KMS, can Redwood operate under a least-privilege model where you never have access to plaintext key material? We want to ensure key material never leaves our control.
2) What does the audit trail look like for model access specifically — can we tie inference requests to user ids and retain those logs for 12 months?
3) If we require EU-only routing with no cross-region failover, will Redwood still meet the Dedicated SLA targets you mentioned?

Happy to take the 30-min technical review — Tue 11/24 at 10am PT works for us. Also, please send any sample contract language around BYOK and key control so our legal team can review before the meeting.

Great — thanks for the quick replies and for scheduling the review. Short answers and next steps: 

- BYOK key control: Yes — for Dedicated/Private we operate under an integration model where the customer maintains key material in their KMS/HSM. Redwood is granted the minimal permissions required (Encrypt/Decrypt or GenerateDataKey) and does not export or persist plaintext key material. We'll provide sample IAM/KMS policy snippets and contract language ahead of the technical call.
- Audit logs / retention: We can emit request-level logs that include a request_id, customer_user_id (if you pass it in), timestamp, model_id, and route. 12-month retention is available for Dedicated as a configurable option; we'll include the pricing delta in the follow-up.
- EU-only routing + SLA: We can pin traffic to EU nodes and disable automatic cross-region failover; SLA targets for Dedicated are achievable with region isolation, though we will note the reduced redundancy in the SLA wording. Ops will propose explicit failover/playbook options in the runbook.

Attached: sample BYOK IAM policy snippet and redwood-kms-architecture.pdf. Agenda for Tue 11/24 10am PT: 1) BYOK flow and IAM policy, 2) audit logging and retention options, 3) EU routing and SLA wording, 4) POC scope. Please share any additional items you want covered.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
